scale.1: Mentioned but materially incomplete, vague, or contradictory
scale.2: Partially specified; major implementation questions remain
scale.3: Clear and substantially complete; minor gaps remain
scale.4: Explicit, measurable, internally consistent, and implementation-ready

categories.label: Problem definition
categories.guidance: Problem, affected users, present pain, and relevant context are explicit.

categories.label: Goals and non-goals
categories.guidance: Outcomes, success measures, scope, and non-goals are bounded.

categories.label: User stories and flows
categories.guidance: Actors, primary journeys, permissions, and alternate flows are covered.

categories.label: Functional requirements
categories.guidance: Behavior is complete, uniquely identifiable, prioritized, and testable.

categories.label: Non-functional requirements
categories.guidance: Performance, reliability, accessibility, compatibility, and scale have measurable targets.

categories.label: Architecture
categories.guidance: Components, responsibilities, data flow, state, and important tradeoffs are defined.

categories.label: Interfaces and contracts
categories.guidance: APIs, schemas, events, errors, versioning, and compatibility rules are explicit.

categories.label: Security and privacy
categories.guidance: Threats, authn/authz, secrets, sensitive data, retention, and abuse cases are addressed.

categories.label: Failure modes
categories.guidance: Expected failures, recovery, retries, timeouts, idempotency, and degraded behavior are specified.

categories.label: Edge cases
categories.guidance: Boundary, empty, duplicate, concurrency, invalid-input, and lifecycle cases are considered.

categories.label: Acceptance criteria
categories.guidance: Requirements map to observable pass/fail criteria, including negative scenarios.

categories.label: Dependencies and constraints
categories.guidance: External systems, owners, assumptions, constraints, and unresolved decisions are named.

categories.label: Observability
categories.guidance: Logs, metrics, traces, audit signals, dashboards, and alerts support operation.

categories.label: Deployment and rollback
categories.guidance: Migration, rollout, feature flags, rollback, and compatibility strategy are safe and explicit.

categories.label: Implementation readiness
categories.guidance: Sequencing, ownership, decisions, artifacts, and definition of done permit autonomous execution.

categories.label: Ambiguity and testability
categories.guidance: Normative language is precise; terms, thresholds, and verification methods are defined.

gates.description: Core behavior or functional requirements are absent
Acceptance criteria are absent or not objectively verifiable
Security/privacy is absent for a security-relevant spec
Ambiguity prevents deterministic implementation or testing

severity.high: Likely causes rework, defects, or operational risk
severity.medium: Meaningful incompleteness with a practical workaround
